items.title: 56706_Buddy Tate oral history interview
items.q: Jimmy Harrison -- they tell me he was a hell of a trombone player.

ctx.x: Then he's the one told me Fletcher wasn't a good business manager and they never made time. You know, he hardly ever got his whole band on the bandstand at one time. Now, I understand they played at Atlantic City Steel Pier and it was hard -- see, that hadn't had no black bands in there. So they wanted Fletcher Henderson, the public kept asking, "Why don't you bring Fletcher Henderson in, man?" said, "he got a band." So the guy said he took a chance and sure enough, he'd open at

eight, nine pieces. Hawk would be in New York, get there late. And said the fella told him, said, "Mr. Henderson," he says, "you got a good band," he says, "but that's the worst conduct band I've ever seen." He says, "And I'm going to have to let you go." He says, "But I love you, really." He says, "But people come here, so and so and so and so," he says, "they got follows."
